title: Power Pages: plugin for GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code edits traditional sites

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: The briefing reports site upload/download UI controls as undocumented even though Microsoft documents them in Visual Studio Code. Its blanket provider-billing statements and claim that administrators cannot distinguish agent uploads also need correction.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 2026-10-23T21:59:27.
Microsoft plans traditional non-SPA site creation and editing through the Power Pages plugin for GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code.
claims.quote: The Power Pages plugin for GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code now supports creating and editing traditional (non-SPA) Power Pages sites.

claims.claim: Developers will be able to create a traditional site using natural-language prompts.
claims.quote: Developers can use natural-language prompts in their AI coding agent to create a new traditional site

claims.claim: Developers will be able to download, inspect and update existing site metadata.
claims.quote: or download, inspect, and update existing site metadata

claims.claim: The planned editable metadata includes web pages, web templates, content snippets, basic and multistep forms, lists, table permissions, web roles and site settings.
claims.quote: such as web pages, web templates, content snippets, basic and multistep forms, lists, table permissions, web roles, and site settings

claims.claim: Changes will be uploaded to the environment using the Power Platform CLI.
claims.quote: then upload changes back to their environment using the Power Platform CLI.

claims.claim: The cited Learn plugin guide describes modern SPA sites.
claims.quote: provides an AI-assisted workflow for creating, deploying, and managing modern single-page application (SPA) sites on Power Pages.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that generated code and configuration can be inaccurate and must be reviewed.
claims.quote: Code and configuration generated by the AI coding agent can be inaccurate. Review, test, and validate all generated content before you approve or deploy it.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Table permissions and web roles control access to Dataverse data, including anonymous access.
claims.quote: Table permissions assigned to web roles allow members of the web role to access data that's stored in Dataverse tables. ... When the Anonymous users web role is granted access to a table, any user who visits the site can access the data in the table.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/assign-table-permissions to sources and cite it for the table-permission and anonymous-access risk.

claims.claim: Downloading site metadata places configuration files on the developer's local machine.
claims.quote: Support for download/upload of website configuration data to/from the local file system

claims.claim: Agent uploads of traditional-site changes happen after developer approval.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages plugin Claude Code approval before upload; read plugin guide and roadmap. The guide requires review as advice and documents some proposal gates, but no universal approval gate for traditional-site uploads.
claims.fix: Replace the assertion with advice: 'Require developers to review and approve proposed changes before upload. Learn says to review, test and validate generated content before approving or deploying it.' Do not promise an enforced traditional-site upload approval gate.

claims.claim: Learn tells developers to review agent proposals before approving them.
claims.quote: Always review agent proposals before approving them.

claims.claim: The workflow uses external coding-agent tools, GitHub Copilot CLI or Claude Code, with Power Platform tooling.
claims.quote: A generative AI coding agent, such as GitHub Copilot CLI or Claude Code, uses this plugin's skills and workflows to complete Power Pages-specific tasks.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Power Platform CLI guidance supports storing site configuration in source control.
claims.quote: You can now check in the website configuration to source control and move the website configuration to any environment using Microsoft Power Platform CLI.

claims.claim: The plugin's licensing model is not yet published, so the model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages plugin GitHub Copilot CLI Claude Code license subscription; Power Pages licensing FAQ plugin pricing. Opened plugin guide and Power Platform licensing FAQs; neither specifies a plugin licensing model.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a plugin-specific charge.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "plugin" "pricing" "Claude"; Power Pages licensing FAQ plugin pricing. Opened plugin guide and Power Platform licensing FAQs and searched their text; no plugin-specific charge is stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: GitHub Copilot subscriptions are separate, outside Microsoft licensing and billed by their provider.
claims.quote: All GitHub usage from that organization — including GitHub Copilot and GitHub Actions — flows to that subscription.
claims.fix: Remove the blanket 'outside Microsoft licensing' and provider-only billing assertion. Say that coding-agent costs depend on the organisation's existing plan and billing arrangement; GitHub Copilot can be billed through a linked Azure subscription. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/reservations/github-pre-purchase.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Claude Code costs are a separate provider-billed subscription outside Microsoft billing.
claims.quote: When you configure Claude Code with Microsoft Foundry, you run the coding agent on Azure infrastructure ... To use Claude models in Microsoft Foundry, you must have a paid Azure subscription
claims.fix: Remove the universal provider-subscription billing statement. Say that Claude Code billing depends on its configured service; Microsoft documents a Microsoft Foundry configuration requiring a paid Azure subscription at https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/how-to/configure-claude-code. Keep plugin-specific licensing as not yet published.

claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in.
claims.quote: Install the Power Pages plugin from the marketplace. ... After you install the plugin, restart Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI to access the plugin's skills as slash commands in your agent session.

claims.claim: No UI surface is documented for downloading and uploading site content.
claims.quote: Power Pages Actions is available in the pane titled Power Pages Actions in the Explorer sidebar of Visual Studio Code. ... Upload: Uploads local changes back to your environment. Download: Downloads the site content to a local folder for offline editing.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui=null with a maker-side Visual Studio Code (Power Platform Tools) entry: 'Explorer > Power Pages Actions > Active Sites > site (right-click) > Download / Upload', citing https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/configure/vs-code-extension#power-pages-actions. Note that this is a developer UI, not a plugin-specific tenant switch.

claims.claim: pac pages download downloads website content from the current Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: pac pages download | Download Power Pages website content from the current Dataverse environment.

claims.claim: pac pages upload uploads website content to the current Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: pac pages upload | Upload Power Pages website content to current Dataverse environment.

claims.claim: pac pages upload-code-site uploads compiled site code.
claims.quote: pac pages upload-code-site | Uploads your compiled code to Power Pages site

claims.claim: The documented developer workflow uses the developer's authenticated Power Platform CLI session.
claims.quote: An authenticated PAC CLI session connected to your target environment. Run pac auth create if you didn't connect yet.

claims.claim: The developer's environment permissions govern access to the Dataverse site configuration.
claims.quote: Table privileges define which tasks a user with access to a table record can do, such as Read, Create, Delete, Write, Assign, Share, Append, and Append To.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/security-roles-privileges for Dataverse role enforcement alongside the CLI authentication guidance. Do not imply that this establishes a separate coding-agent permission model.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a tenant admin UI or API switch specifically for this coding-agent plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages plugin admin disable tenant switch; "Power Pages" "plugin" disable PowerShell API tenant setting. Opened plugin guide and Copilot hub for Power Pages; neither documents a plugin-specific switch. Search results describe other controls.

claims.claim: Code sites also use the Power Platform CLI upload/download workflow.
claims.quote: Power Pages SPA sites are managed using the PAC CLI commands upload-code-site and download-code-site.

claims.claim: Nothing in the admin center distinguishes coding-agent uploads from manual uploads.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages plugin audit logs; Power Pages plugin audit admin center. Read plugin guide, Copilot hub and View Power Pages activity logs in Microsoft Purview; none states that agent and manual uploads cannot be distinguished.
claims.fix: Replace the categorical assertion with 'Microsoft has not documented a plugin-specific upload identifier in the admin center at the time of writing (November 2026).' Keep the plugin audit-trail question open; do not conclude that identification is impossible.

claims.where: Open questions: existing security review skills
claims.claim: The existing plugin has security review skills.
claims.quote: Run security review | /security-review | Orchestrates the focused security skills and consolidates every finding into a single HTML report.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to run table-permission audits, but the controls table has no permission-review row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Run table permission audits after agent changes.' Table rows: 'Downloading and uploading site content and code' and 'Admin switch for the coding-agent plugin'.
claims.fix: Add a site-scoped table-permission review row. The documented manual UI is Power Pages site > Security > Table permissions > table (...) > Edit, at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/assign-table-permissions. The plugin guide also documents /audit-permissions for its current SPA workflow; explicitly leave traditional-site applicability unconfirmed.
